api/SmartUIScaler.SmartUIFramingBounds.h.summary: Class SmartUIFramingBounds Namespace SmartUIScaler Assembly SmartUIScaler.dll Describes the volume of a character or an object that a SmartUIWorldFollower keeps inside its target rectangle, or that a SmartUIMeshFitter fits into its parent RectTransform instead of measuring the Renderers. The volume is typed in by hand, so it can cover the animations and poses the object will use and does not change while they play. The values are in the space of the nearest SmartUIWorldFollower or SmartUIMeshFitter found on this GameObject or its parents, so framing bounds on equipment held in an animated hand stay still. All enabled framing bounds on that GameObject and its children are combined: equipping an item that has framing bounds of its own widens the framing, and removing it narrows the framing again. The values can be changed at runtime, also by animation clips. api/SmartUIScaler.SmartUIMeshFitter.html.summary: Class SmartUIMeshFitter Namespace SmartUIScaler Assembly SmartUIScaler.dll Sizes and places a 3D object, for example a mesh or a whole model, inside the parent RectTransform, so it scales with the UI like any UI element. The bounds of all enabled Renderers on this GameObject and its children are fitted into the parent rectangle after the UIScalers are updated each frame. When SmartUIFramingBounds are found on this GameObject or its children, their typed-in volume is fitted instead, so an animated model keeps the same size while it moves. The back of the bounds is placed on the parent rectangle and moved toward the camera by Depth Offset, measured in UI units, so the depth and the offset scale together with the width and the height. Position and scale of the Transform are set by this component. Rotate a child object instead of this one: rotating this one around X or Y can skew it, because UIScalers do not scale depth. 3D objects are drawn under Screen Space Camera and World Space canvases, not under Screen Space Overlay canvases. api/SmartUIScaler.SmartUIWorldFollower.h.title: Class SmartUIWorldFollower | Smart UI Scaler plugin
api/SmartUIScaler.SmartUIWorldFollower.h.summary: Class SmartUIWorldFollower Namespace SmartUIScaler Assembly SmartUIScaler.dll Shows a world object inside a RectTransform through a camera of its own, for example a 3D model in a shop slot that lives inside a UIScaler. After the UIScalers are updated each frame the camera projection is shifted so the object's focus point lands in the center of the target rectangle and the camera's field of view (or orthographic size) covers the target height. With Move Camera on, the camera is also placed Distance behind the focus point along its forward direction, so the object is seen head-on. With Move Camera off, the camera transform is left to something else, for example Cinemachine, and only the projection follows the target. With Clip To Target on, the camera viewport is set to the on-screen part of the target, so nothing outside the target is drawn and a target partly off-screen is cut, not squeezed. Turn it off for an overlay camera in a URP camera stack, which ignores its own viewport: the camera then draws its whole viewport and its culling mask must show only the object. The camera belongs to this follower: give it a higher depth than the main camera or add it to the camera stack, and depth only clearing. A target with zero width or height is a point: the object is placed on it and the field of view (or orthographic size) covers the camera viewport height as usual. A camera with a target texture works in that texture's pixels, so the object can be shown in a target inside a Screen Space Camera canvas that renders into the same texture. When SmartUIFramingBounds are found on this GameObject or its children, the projection is also zoomed so their combined volume fits the target, Framing Padding away from its edges, and the center of that volume is used instead of the focus point. The camera's position, rotation and field of view then only decide the viewing angle and the perspective, not the size of the object. api/SmartUIScaler.html.summary: Namespace SmartUIScaler Classes CoreUIScaler Base class of UIScaler components with core scaling logic. SmartUIAspectFitter Fits its RectTransform into the parent RectTransform with a fixed aspect ratio or the aspect ratio of its Image or RawImage, anywhere between fitting inside the parent and covering it. SmartUIAspectSwitch Switches aspect variants by the aspect ratio of a UIScaler screen area. Listens to the UIScaler on the same object, or the first parent one, and on every resize activates the layout of the matching variant and deactivates the layouts of the other variants. Objects that are not listed as layouts are left untouched. When the active variant changes the deactivated and activated events of the variants are invoked, then the Active Variant Changed event with the name of the new variant, then the listeners added with AddActiveVariantChangedListener(Action<UIScalerAspectVariant>, bool), so any other way of switching can be wired in the inspector or from code. In the editor layouts are switched and the inspector events invoked only in Preview scaling mode, the active variant is resolved in every mode. SmartUICanvasScaler UIScaler that fits its RectTransform into the pixel area of the Canvas it is placed under. SmartUIExpander Expands its RectTransform from the parent RectTransform to the chosen borders of the Canvas. The whole RectTransform is driven by this component and recalculated on every resize: it covers the parent rectangle, and the chosen edges reach the Canvas borders. SmartUIFramingBounds Describes the volume of a character or an object that a SmartUIWorldFollower keeps inside its target rectangle, or that a SmartUIMeshFitter fits into its parent RectTransform instead of measuring the Renderers. The volume is typed in by hand, so it can cover the animations and poses the object will use and does not change while they play. The values are in the space of the nearest SmartUIWorldFollower or SmartUIMeshFitter found on this GameObject or its parents, so framing bounds on equipment held in an animated hand stay still. All enabled framing bounds on that GameObject and its children are combined: equipping an item that has framing bounds of its own widens the framing, and removing it narrows the framing again. The values can be changed at runtime, also by animation clips. SmartUIManager Entry point for external code that needs to stay in sync with UIScaler updates. Drives UIScaler updates in play mode and in edit mode. Created automatically and must not be added to a GameObject manually. SmartUIMeshFitter Sizes and places a 3D object, for example a mesh or a whole model, inside the parent RectTransform, so it scales with the UI like any UI element. The bounds of all enabled Renderers on this GameObject and its children are fitted into the parent rectangle after the UIScalers are updated each frame. When SmartUIFramingBounds are found on this GameObject or its children, their typed-in volume is fitted instead, so an animated model keeps the same size while it moves. The back of the bounds is placed on the parent rectangle and moved toward the camera by Depth Offset, measured in UI units, so the depth and the offset scale together with the width and the height. Position and scale of the Transform are set by this component. Rotate a child object instead of this one: rotating this one around X or Y can skew it, because UIScalers do not scale depth. 3D objects are drawn under Screen Space Camera and World Space canvases, not under Screen Space Overlay canvases. SmartUISizeLimiter Fits its RectTransform into the parent RectTransform with a fixed reference height and a limited aspect ratio. SmartUIWorldFollower Shows a world object inside a RectTransform through a camera of its own, for example a 3D model in a shop slot that lives inside a UIScaler. After the UIScalers are updated each frame the camera projection is shifted so the object's focus point lands in the center of the target rectangle and the camera's field of view (or orthographic size) covers the target height. With Move Camera on, the camera is also placed Distance behind the focus point along its forward direction, so the object is seen head-on. With Move Camera off, the camera transform is left to something else, for example Cinemachine, and only the projection follows the target. With Clip To Target on, the camera viewport is set to the on-screen part of the target, so nothing outside the target is drawn and a target partly off-screen is cut, not squeezed. Turn it off for an overlay camera in a URP camera stack, which ignores its own viewport: the camera then draws its whole viewport and its culling mask must show only the object. The camera belongs to this follower: give it a higher depth than the main camera or add it to the camera stack, and depth only clearing. A target with zero width or height is a point: the object is placed on it and the field of view (or orthographic size) covers the camera viewport height as usual. A camera with a target texture works in that texture's pixels, so the object can be shown in a target inside a Screen Space Camera canvas that renders into the same texture. When SmartUIFramingBounds are found on this GameObject or its children, the projection is also zoomed so their combined volume fits the target, Framing Padding away from its edges, and the center of that volume is used instead of the focus point. The camera's position, rotation and field of view then only decide the viewing angle and the perspective, not the size of the object. UIScalerBehaviour Base class of every UIScaler related components. UIScalerGroupSo UIScaler group scriptable object. UIScalerGroups UIScaler groups manager. UIScalerGroupsPersistenceManager Loads the UIScaler group options from PlayerPrefs on Awake and saves them when the application is paused or quit. UIScalerGroupsSaveData UIScaler groups save data. UIScalerGroupsSaveData.UIScalerGroupOptions UIScaler group options save data. Structs UIScalerAspectVariant Named aspect ratio band of a SmartUIAspectSwitch. The variant with the largest MinAspectRatio that is not wider than the UIScaler screen area becomes active; a screen area thinner than every variant activates the thinnest one. The Layout object is the default way of switching, the events allow any other reaction to be wired in the inspector. UIScalerOptions UIScaler options. Enums FramingShape Shape of the volume described by SmartUIFramingBounds. MeshFitMode How SmartUIMeshFitter sizes an object inside the parent RectTransform. SafeAreaSymmetry Controls which safe area insets are mirrored to the opposite side of the screen. UIScalerAlignment Used for aligning UIScaler inside provided screen area.

index.html.title: Introduction | Smart UI Scaler plugin
index.html.summary: Introduction Smart UI Scaler makes one Unity UI (uGUI) layout fit every screen. Design your UI once at a reference resolution, and Smart UI Scaler fits it into any screen size, aspect ratio, safe area or camera viewport, growing it toward the edges exactly as far as you allow. No more choosing between a layout that is cut off on phones and one that floats in the middle of an ultra wide monitor. Why not the Canvas Scaler? Unity's Canvas Scaler scales the whole canvas by one rule. Everything stretches or shrinks together, wide screens get empty margins or cropped edges, the safe area is your problem, and a single canvas cannot serve a split screen. Smart UI Scaler works per Rect Transform instead: each scaler is a rectangle with its own reference resolution and its own rules, and you can have as many of them as your screen needs. What you get 📐 Design once, ship everywhere Build the UI at your reference resolution and keep it readable from a phone in portrait to a 32:9 monitor. 🛡️ Safe area done for you The UI stays inside the notch and home indicator insets, follows rotation and can stay centered when the inset is only on one side, while bars and backgrounds still reach the real screen edges. 📏 You decide how the UI expands Choose how far the layout grows from its designed size toward the full screen and where it sits on the screen, and keep parts of it, such as a lobby or a card grid, between two aspect ratios. 🔀 A layout per screen shape When one layout cannot serve every screen, give phones in portrait, tablets and wide monitors each a layout of their own. The right one is picked by the shape of the screen, and you edit each layout in its real shape. Images and backgrounds keep their proportions on every screen, never stretched. 🧊 3D objects in the UI Lit 3D backgrounds, titles, spinning items and characters keep their place and size on every screen, like any other UI element. A character or an item can also be shown through a camera of its own, and it stays framed while it animates or changes equipment. 🎚️ A UI scale slider for your players Let players make the UI smaller or larger while it keeps covering the same area. Bind it to a settings slider and the whole HUD follows. 🧩 Several scalers on one screen HUD, menus, popups and split screen viewports each scale on their own terms. Scalers can be nested and mixed with regular UI in the same canvas. 💾 Shared settings that persist Group scalers through assets, change their options at runtime and keep them between sessions with the built-in PlayerPrefs persistence or your own save system. 🛠️ See it before you press Play The layout looks the same in Edit Mode and in Play Mode. Preview any aspect ratio, simulate safe areas and switch between device presets from one editor window. ⚡ Nothing to pay per frame Scalers resize only when the screen, the safe area or their options change. In a steady frame the plugin only checks that nothing changed, with no allocations. 🔌 Extensible Write custom scalers for render textures, read scaler sizes in the same frame through an update event, and learn from seventeen demo scenes that cover every feature. What is included Smart UI Canvas Scaler, Smart UI Expander, Smart UI Size Limiter, Smart UI Aspect Fitter and Smart UI Aspect Switch components Smart UI Mesh Fitter, Smart UI World Follower and Smart UI Framing Bounds components for 3D objects in the UI UI Scaler Groups with runtime API and PlayerPrefs persistence Smart UI Scaler editor window with safe area simulation and presets Seventeen demo scenes, from a single scaler to 3D objects in the UI and custom scalers Full source code, online manual and scripting API, offline PDFs Requirements ❗ Unity 2022.3.0 or newer, tested up to Unity 6000.6 ❗ Unity UI (uGUI) canvases, Screen Space Overlay and Screen Space Camera. UI Toolkit is not supported.

manual/3d_objects_in_ui.html.title: 3D objects in the UI | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/3d_objects_in_ui.html.summary: 3D objects in the UI Smart UI Scaler has two components that bring 3D objects into a layout that follows every screen shape, and one component that describes the volume they fit. They look similar, but each one changes something different. This page helps you choose. Which one do I need? The Smart UI Mesh Fitter makes the 3D object part of the UI: it is placed and sized inside a Rect Transform like any other UI element and drawn by the camera of the canvas. The Smart UI World Follower turns a Rect Transform into a window into a 3D world: the object stays where it is in its scene, and its own camera shows it in the Rect Transform. Many objects, such as an item in an inventory, work with both. These questions decide: Question If yes Is the canvas Screen Space Overlay? Smart UI World Follower. The Mesh Fitter cannot draw 3D objects on Screen Space Overlay canvases. Should the object be lit by lights of its own or use camera effects of its own, separate from the UI? Or does it belong to a scene, such as a character standing in a room? Smart UI World Follower Otherwise: the canvas is Screen Space Camera or World Space, and the object is lit together with the UI Smart UI Mesh Fitter. It needs no extra camera, so it also suits many objects at once. Left, part of the UI: two Smart UI Mesh Fitters size the 3D objects like UI elements. The tiled wall is set to Envelope and covers the whole screen at the proportions of its texture, resizing with every screen shape, and the emblem is set to Fit in a slot that stays in the center of the UI Scaler. The canvas is Screen Space Camera, so both are lit together with the rest of the UI and the emblem casts its shadow on the wall. Right, a window into a 3D world: the character belongs to a room with lights of its own, so a Smart UI World Follower shows it through its own camera in the free space between the menu panels. Then, if the object changes its size through animations, poses or equipment, add Smart UI Framing Bounds to describe the volume that must always fit. It is not a third choice: it adds to either component. Comparison Smart UI Mesh Fitter Smart UI World Follower What it changes The object: its position and scale The camera's projection, and with Move Camera also its position Where the object lives Under a Rect Transform inside the canvas Anywhere in the scene Camera The camera of the canvas A camera of its own, or the scene camera Size of the object in its scene Changes with the UI Stays the same, the view zooms instead Lights Lit together with the rest of the UI Lit by its own scene or lights of its own Screen Space Overlay canvas Not drawn Works Extra rendering cost None One camera per follower, unless the scene camera is used With Smart UI Framing Bounds The typed-in volume is fitted instead of the measured Renderer bounds, so an animated model keeps its size The view zooms so the typed-in volume fits the Target, including equipment with framing bounds of its own Typical use Lit backgrounds, emblems, 3D icons, coins, chests, items in slots and item inspectors Character screens, a character in a room between menu panels, item inspectors with lights of their own Examples You want Use A lit background that covers the screen at the proportions of its texture Mesh Fitter set to Envelope, on a quad with the aspect ratio of its texture A 3D logo on that background that casts a shadow on it Mesh Fitter set to Fit, with a Depth Offset Rotating 3D icons, such as a coin next to the coin counter or an item in each slot of a shop grid Mesh Fitter with Use Bounding Sphere in each slot, rotating a child object. On a Screen Space Overlay canvas: World Follower with a camera of its own per slot An item inspector where the player rotates and zooms an item, as in an RPG inventory Mesh Fitter with Use Bounding Sphere, rotating a child object, zoomed by resizing its slot. On a Screen Space Overlay canvas or with lights of its own: World Follower with Framing Bounds set to Sphere, zoomed by changing the Radius A 3D title, tilted or gently swaying Mesh Fitter set to Fit in the title slot, rotating a child object. For a swaying title, Framing Bounds set to Box around its movement; Use Bounding Sphere would shrink a wide title A character in a room that stays between the menu panels and fully visible while it equips a long sword World Follower on the scene camera with Clip To Target and Move Camera off, plus Framing Bounds on the character and on the sword Combining them Mesh Fitter and World Follower are not used on the same object. A scene can use both: a lit background with a Mesh Fitter behind the menu, and a character in a 3D room through a World Follower. Smart UI Aspect Fitter is the 2D counterpart: it keeps images and Rect Transforms at their aspect ratio. The Fit and Envelope modes of the Mesh Fitter do the same for 3D objects. Demo scenes Demo 13 - Mesh Fitter: a lit tiled wall and an emblem that casts a shadow on it. Demo 14 - World Follower: objects in shop cards, each through a camera of its own. Demo 15 - Character Framing: a dress-up screen with a character in a room, equipment and framing bounds.

manual/custom_ui_scaler.html.title: Custom UI Scaler | Smart UI Scaler plugin
manual/custom_ui_scaler.html.summary: Custom UI Scaler A custom UI Scaler is needed when the parent Canvas has "Screen Space Camera" Render Mode and the attached camera renders into a Render Texture. The Smart UI Canvas Scaler component cannot know where the rendered image ends up on the screen, so a custom UI Scaler provides that information. Demo 17 contains a complete implementation, RenderTextureUIScaler, for a canvas rendered into a Render Texture and shown by a RawImage. Use it as the reference for the steps below. Implementation Extend CoreUIScaler and implement these two methods: Provide the screen space Rect of the area where the Render Texture is shown. protected abstract Rect GetScreenRect() Convert a screen space Rect to a world space Rect inside the Render Texture's Canvas. protected abstract Rect ScreenRectToWorldRect(Rect screenRect) Mark the class with [ExecuteAlways] so that the custom UI Scaler also works in Edit Mode, like the built-in components do. Detecting changes A UI Scaler resizes only when its Rect Transform has changed, which is what happens when the Canvas resizes. When the provided screen Rect can change on its own, for example because the RawImage moves on the screen, the custom UI Scaler has to request a resize itself. Override OnPreWillRenderCanvases, compare the current screen Rect with the previous one and set transform.hasChanged = true before calling the base method: protected override void OnPreWillRenderCanvases() { var screenRect = GetScreenRect(); if (screenRect != _lastScreenRect) { _lastScreenRect = screenRect; transform.hasChanged = true; } base.OnPreWillRenderCanvases(); } Inspector The Group and Options fields of a UI Scaler are drawn by a custom inspector. To show them on a custom UI Scaler, add a nested editor class that extends CoreUIScalerEditor and append the custom fields after the base inspector: #if UNITY_EDITOR [UnityEditor.CustomEditor(typeof(MyUIScaler))] class Editor : CoreUIScalerEditor { public override void OnInspectorGUI() { base.OnInspectorGUI(); serializedObject.Update(); UnityEditor.EditorGUILayout.PropertyField(serializedObject.FindProperty("_outputImage")); serializedObject.ApplyModifiedProperties(); } } #endif Safe area The "Use Safe Area" option intersects the provided screen Rect with the screen's safe area, so it only makes sense when the screen Rect is in real screen coordinates. Demo 17 uses it this way: the inner UI Scaler only occupies the part of the image that is inside both the screen and the safe area. Turn the option off when the output is not shown directly on the screen.
